summary: The note argues that local political parties should treat public health with transparency, accountability and technology ahead of the municipal elections due November 15, 2023. It surveys proposals from parties in Cedarville and Brookfield, including a Transparent Health Initiative, a Green Spaces Initiative and a telehealth program, and praises cross-party collaboration in Belltown. It concludes that the elections are a pivotal moment for redefining the relationship between political entities and citizens.
one_line: Local parties' public health platforms ahead of the November 15, 2023 municipal elections are examined, stressing transparency, technology, accountability and bipartisan collaboration.
key_facts: Municipal elections are due on November 15, 2023.

Jane Doe of the Meadowlands Health First Party (MHFP) proposed a "Transparent Health Initiative", reported September 10, 2023, to increase funding for local clinics and give citizens real-time access to public health data.

The Sustainable Health and Prosperity Party (SHAPP) in Brookfield promises to increase green cover by 20% and reduce urban pollution levels by 30% by 2026, per chairperson Michael Johnson on October 7, 2023.

The Citizens' Wellness Coalition (CWC) proposed a "Green Spaces Initiative" to promote parks and community gardens to enhance mental health, as outlined by policy director Sarah Thompson at a town hall on September 25, 2023.
The MHFP's initiative would distribute clear information on public health risks, hospital capacities and availability of essential services, which the note calls an "open book policy".
The Brookfield Connected Care Program (BCCP), backed by SHAPP, uses telehealth to connect rural areas with specialists in metropolitan centers.
Mike Green, SHAPP's innovation lead, championed the BCCP plan on September 30, 2023, including mobile health clinics equipped with telemedicine technologies.

Mayor Andrew Gomez of Belltown organized a bipartisan roundtable on October 15, 2023 on the urban spread of communicable diseases, leading to a historic collaboration between parties traditionally at odds.
The note says accountability requires clear benchmarks for success and channels for public feedback and criticism.
The note says advocacy coalitions, community leaders and patient groups can shape policy agendas and parties must collaborate with them.
